contests.title: Brown Deer School District — Question II — School improvement bonds

provenance.quote:
BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the School District of Brown Deer,
Milwaukee County, Wisconsin that there shall be issued pursuant to Chapter 67 of the Wisconsin
Statutes, general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $35,000,000 for the public purpose
of paying the cost of a school facility improvement project consisting of: district-wide capital
maintenance, building infrastructure, energy efficiency and accessibility improvements,
including elevator replacement and playground renovations at the Elementary School;
renovations at the Middle/High School, including to classrooms, the auditorium, pool and locker
rooms; site improvements, including replacing the track and adding turf to the field at the
Middle/High School; and acquisition of furnishings, fixtures and equipment.

contests.title: Brown Deer School District — Question I — Temporary school-revenue increase

provenance.quote:
BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the School District of Brown Deer,
Milwaukee County, Wisconsin that the revenues included in the School District budget be
authorized to exceed the revenue limit specified in Section 121.91, Wisconsin Statutes, by
$2,800,000 per year for five years, beginning with the 2026-2027 school year and ending with
the 2030-2031 school year, for non-recurring purposes consisting of operational and maintenance
expenses, including teacher and staff compensation.

contests.title: Evansville Community School District — Temporary school-revenue increase

provenance.quote:
BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the Evansville Community School District, Rock, Green and Dane Counties, Wisconsin that the revenues included in the School District budget be authorized to exceed the revenue limit specified in Section 121.91, Wisconsin Statutes, by $5,300,000 per year for four years, beginning with the 2027-2028 school year and ending with the 2030-2031 school year, for non-recurring purposes consisting of operational and maintenance expenses, including to provide student resources and educational programming and to address facility maintenance.
Adopted and recorded August 12, 2026.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the district to borrow up to $35 million through general obligation bonds for school improvements. The projects include maintenance, infrastructure, energy efficiency and accessibility across the district; an elementary-school elevator and playground; middle/high-school classrooms, auditorium, pool and locker rooms; a replacement track and turf field; and furnishings, fixtures and equipment.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve borrowing up to $35 million for these projects.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the district to raise $2.8 million a year above Wisconsin’s school-revenue limit for five school years, from 2026–27 through 2030–31. The money is for operations and maintenance, including teacher and staff compensation. This temporary authorization ends after those years.

Allows the district to raise $5.3 million a year above Wisconsin’s school-revenue limit for four school years, from 2027–28 through 2030–31. It would pay for operations and maintenance, including student resources, educational programs, and facility maintenance. This temporary authorization ends after those years.

Allows the district to raise money above Wisconsin’s school-revenue limit for four school years: $29 million in 2027–28, $36 million in 2028–29, $44 million in 2029–30, and $49 million in 2030–31. The money is for educational programs, staffing, and other operating expenses. This temporary authorization ends after those years.

Allows the district to borrow up to $35 million through general obligation bonds for school maintenance and improvements, safety and security projects, other school-site improvements, and furnishings, fixtures and equipment.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve borrowing up to $35 million for these projects.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the district to raise $5 million a year above Wisconsin’s school-revenue limit for four school years, from 2027–28 through 2030–31. It would pay for class sizes, instructional programs, staff recruitment and retention, student mental health support, educational technology, transportation, and other educational expenses. This temporary authorization ends after those years.
